# EMF (Enshrouded Modding Framework): a summary for AI agents

Generated by tools/gen_llms_txt.py from the repository's headers, sources and docs. Do not edit by hand.

EMF is a native mod framework for the game Enshrouded (Windows, Vulkan). A dinput8.dll proxy loads
<game>\emf\emf_core.dll, which loads mods from <game>\emf\mods\<id>\ (a folder with mod.json and a DLL, or
main.lua for a Lua mod). Mods get a C API (EmfApi, version 40); C++ wraps it in sdk/include/emf/emf.hpp.
Key facts:
- Gameplay changes happen on the host's SERVER world (your own game or the one you host); a client of someone
  else's game only sees results. Touch ECS data only inside world callbacks (on_tick, run_on_world, on_event,
  commands), on the world passed in. Component pointers are valid only during that callback.
- Settings: <game>\emf\config\<id>.ini, section [<id>]; the in-game console (key under Esc) has a Mods tab.
- Log: <game>\emf\emf_core.log (truncated at every game start). Lines from a mod start with [<id>].
- Lua mods reload within a second of saving a .lua file or mod.json; a script error pauses the mod, never
  the game.
- Docs: docs/modding/README.md (start), first_mod.md (Lua in 10 minutes), lua.md, reference.md (every API
  function with C++ names and rules), cookbook.md, debug_bridge.md, ai_agents.md. Rules for agents: AGENTS.md.

## C API (sdk/include/emf/emf_api.h, EmfApi version 40)

A mod DLL exports: extern "C" __declspec(dllexport) bool emf_mod_load(const EmfApi* api). Fields are only
appended (check api->size before using a later one). Refusals return NULL/0/false and log a line.

### v1
- uint32_t version: EMF_API_VERSION of the core
- uint32_t size: sizeof(EmfApi) of the core
- void log(const char* mod, const char* fmt, ...): printf-style line into emf/emf_core.log, prefixed with the mod name.
- EmfWorld* server_world(void): Most recently ticking world of a kind, or NULL (no server world on a client of someone else's game).
- EmfWorld* client_world(void)
- uint8_t world_kind(EmfWorld* world)
- uint32_t world_tick(EmfWorld* world): The world's tick counter.
- int64_t ecs_time_ns(EmfWorld* world): Current ECS time in ns (tick * tick length), what game programs see as "now".
- void* singleton(EmfWorld* world, const char* name): Named world singleton (e.g. "g38_daytime::Daytime"), or NULL.
- uint32_t local_player(void): Local player's EntityId from the client world (LocalPlayerData+4), or 0.
- void* get_component(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t hash, uint32_t entity, uint64_t* size_out): Component data of an entity by its types.json qualifiedHash, or NULL.
- void for_each_entity(EmfWorld* world, EmfEntityCallback cb, void* user): Calls cb for every entity id in the world (snapshot taken first).
- void on_tick(EmfWorldCallback cb, void* user): cb runs after every simulation step of every world (server, prediction, client).
- void run_on_world(uint8_t kind, EmfWorldCallback cb, void* user): cb runs once, after the next simulation step of a world of `kind`.
- void* resolve(const char* sig_name): Address of a resolved engine signature by name (see src/common/signatures.cpp), or NULL.
- bool hook(const char* sig_name, void* detour, void** original): Hooks a resolved signature by name and enables it.

### v2
- bool hook_program(const char* name, EmfProgramCallback pre, EmfProgramCallback post, void* user): Wraps an ECS program's update function by program name (see docs/ecs_programs.md): pre(ctx,user) runs before the game's update ...
- bool register_program(const char* name, uint8_t world_kind, EmfProgramCallback fn, void* user): Adds a mod ECS "system program": fn(ctx,user) runs once per tick on worlds of `world_kind` (EMF_WORLD_SERVER = host only ...
- uint32_t spawn(EmfWorld* world, const uint8_t template_guid[16], double x, double y, double z): Spawns a template (16-byte GUID as stored in the game) at (x,y,z) meters and returns the new entity id, or 0 (logged) if refused.
- bool destroy(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t entity): Destroys an entity on a SERVER world (same calling rules as spawn).
- void on_save(EmfSaveCallback cb, void* user): cb(world_slot_id) after the host wrote a world save (runs on the game's save thread).
- void on_load(EmfSaveCallback cb, void* user): cb(world_slot_id) after the host loaded a world save, before the world starts (server thread).

### v3
- bool register_program_def(const EmfProgramDef* def): Like register_program, plus the events the program reads (events_in) and sends (events_out).
- void* emit_event(void* program_context, const char* event_name, uint32_t expected_size): Inside the program's own callback only, with the program_context passed to it: sends one event declared in events_out.
- uint32_t read_events(void* program_context, const char* event_name, uint32_t expected_size, EmfEventCallback cb, void* user): Inside the program's own callback only: calls cb for each event of this type the game queued for this tick (declared in events_in).

### v4
- bool on_event(uint8_t world_kind, const char* event_name, uint32_t expected_size, EmfWorldEventCallback cb, void* user): cb(world, event, size, user) for every engine event `event_name` (short type name, e.g. "EntityDiedEvent", "HitEvent", "PickupEvent") that ...

### v5
- void for_each_item(EmfWorld* world, EmfItemCallback cb, void* user): The game's item definitions, from the world's item registry (any world).
- uint32_t find_item(EmfWorld* world, const char* name): Item id by the game's debug name: exact match first, else the first case-insensitive one.
- bool item_info(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t item_id, EmfItemInfo* out): Fills *out (out->size must be at least sizeof(EmfItemInfo)); false for an unknown item.
- uint32_t give_item(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t player, uint32_t item_id, uint32_t count): Drops count (1..65535) x item as a loose pickup 1 m above `player`; the game's own loot code puts it in the inventory of whoever picks it ...
- uint32_t spawn_ex(EmfWorld* world, const uint8_t template_guid[16], double x, double y, double z, const EmfComponentInit* components, uint32_t count): spawn with up to 15 extra spawn components after the transform (e.g. a Level or PickupItem).

### v6
- bool register_command(const char* name, const char* help, EmfCommandCallback cb, void* user): Adds a command typed into the EMF console window or emf/commands.txt.
- void command_reply(const char* fmt, ...): printf-style line back to whoever typed the running command (console window and core log).

### v7
- void* get_template_component(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t hash, uint32_t entity, uint64_t* size_out): The entity's template data for a component (types.json qualifiedHash), e.g. ActiveNpcState or Enemy01BehaviorState: the defaults every ...
- void* item_data(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t item_id, uint64_t* size_out): The game's ItemInfo for an item in this world's registry (*size_out = 2088), or NULL.
- bool set_item_max_stack(uint32_t item_id, uint16_t max): Sets an item's maximum stack size (1-65535) in every live world (server and client).
- bool write_memory(void* dst, const void* src, uint64_t n): Copies n bytes into game DATA, e.g. a field of get_template_component or item_data.

### v9
- uint32_t server_session(void): Number of the hosted session: 0 before the first server world, +1 each time a server world is set up (a new game, a reload, another world).

### v14

- bool hook_pattern(const char* name, const EmfPattern* pattern, void* detour, void** original): find_pattern + hook: `detour` replaces the function found; *original (may be NULL) gets the way to call the original, set before the hook ...

- bool game_build(EmfGameBuild* out): Which game build runs.

### v15

### v23
- bool change_component(EmfWorld* world, const EmfComponentChange* change): Adds a component to an entity, or removes one, through the engine's own command.

### v24
- bool window_open(const EmfWindowDef* def): Opens a window drawn by EMF's overlay (copied, every string too).
- bool window_update(const EmfWindowDef* def): New contents for the open window def->id (cb and user are ignored; the scroll stays).
- bool window_close(const char* id): Closes the window `id`; its cb gets CLOSED (BY_MOD).

### v25

### v27
- bool net_channel(const EmfNetChannel* def): A channel of your mod; false (logged) for a bad definition or a name that is taken.
- bool net_to_server(const char* channel, const void* data, uint32_t size): A player's game -> the server.
- bool net_to_player(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t player, const char* channel, const void* data, uint32_t size): The server -> one player's game (`player`: its entity in the server world).
- uint32_t net_to_players(EmfWorld* world, const char* channel, const void* data, uint32_t size): The server -> every player whose game has the channel (the host's own game included): how many.
- uint32_t net_peer(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t player, const char* channel): The channel version a player's game has (server: world, player), or the server's (a player's game: NULL, 0); 0 = none.

### v28
- bool on_player(EmfPlayerCallback cb, void* user): `cb` for each player who joins, leaves or dies on the server world (the host's game or a dedicated server; its thread, after its step).

### v40
- uint32_t enemy_move(EmfWorld* world, EmfMoveOrder* order, EmfMoveCallback cb, void* user): Walks order->enemy to its points (see EMF_MOVE_*).
- bool enemy_move_cancel(uint32_t id): Ends a move (its callback gets EMF_MOVE_CANCELLED): at once inside a world callback on the server world, else at the next step.
- uint32_t enemy_moving(EmfWorld* world, uint32_t enemy): The id of `enemy`'s move, 0 = it is not moving.

### Constants

## Lua (the lua mod; docs/modding/lua.md)

mod.json has "main": "main.lua" and "depends": {"lua": ">=1.33"} (the Lua host is 1.33.0). Callbacks get a
`world` valid only during the callback. world:get(component, id) returns a component as a table with its real
field names (sdk/include/emf/generated/components.hpp); assigning a field writes the game's data.

- `emf.id`: your mod's id
- `emf.dir`: your mod's folder (for your own data files)
- `emf.log(...)` / `print(...)`: a line in `emf\emf_core.log` (and the console), prefixed `[id]`
- `emf.notify(text)`: a note at the top of the screen for a few seconds
- `emf.hud(id, text [, place [, rgba]])`: a line kept on screen; `""` removes it; place `"top_right"` (below the quest tracker), `"bottom_right"` or `"bottom_left"` (or 0, 1, 2), so a `select` setting's value fits; `rgba` a `color` setting's `"#rrggbb"`, `"#rrggbbaa"` (with alpha: a line can fade), a number like `0xFFD070FF` or the text `"0xFFD070FF"`; 0 (or none) means the usual colour; the player can move, scale and hide each place in the HUD editor
- `emf.on_tick(fn)`: `fn(world)` after every world step (server, client). In a game you host, a client step leaves your mod out while it is still busy in the server step (at most 30 steps in a row), so the game's frame seldom waits for your server work (it still does when your mod has a client bus callback with messages due, a client `on_event`, or after 30 steps); keep heavy work in the server world
- `emf.bus.subscribe(topic, fn [, world])`: (1.17) listen for a topic in `"server"` (default) or `"client"` world; `fn(world, source_mod_id, payload)` runs on that world's next step when a publication arrives; true when registered
- `emf.bus.publish(topic, payload [, world])`: (1.17) queue a copy of a text/binary payload for `"server"` (default) or `"client"`; true when queued, false if the topic, payload or queue limit is invalid (logged once per rejection streak)
- `emf.bus.unsubscribe(topic)`: (1.17) remove all this mod's callbacks for a topic in both worlds; true if any were removed, false if none existed
- `emf.json.encode(value)`: (1.18) a Lua value as JSON text; nil plus a message when it cannot be written (see "JSON (1.18)")
- `emf.json.decode(text)`: (1.18) JSON text as a Lua value; nil plus a message when the text is not valid JSON
- `emf.json.null`: (1.18) the value `decode` gives for JSON `null` and `encode` writes as `null` (a Lua table cannot hold nil)
- `emf.on_event(name, fn [, "server"/"client"])`: `fn(world, event)` for each engine event `name`, with its fields as a table (see below); call it at the top of `main.lua`
- `emf.command(name, help, fn [, {players = true}])`: a console command `<id>.<name>` (1.6: a `name` that is exactly your mod's id is the command `<id>` itself); `fn(world, args)` (`args` is a table of words); answer with `emf.reply(text)`. The full name is 1-32 letters, digits, `_ . -` (with `<id>.`) and ignores case; another name is not added: false and a log line, the rest of the mod runs. `{players = true}` (1.4): every player may run it from the game's chat, not only the `[chat] admins` ([server.md](server.md)); use it for commands that read or act on their sender (`emf.sender()`). A reload can add or take off the mark. Write `help` as `<args>: what it does` (`"<name>: call a beast"`, `": your life skills"`): the console shows it as players type and offers `a|b` choices and item names for an `<item>` argument
- `emf.local_player()`: your player's entity id
- `emf.sender()`: inside a command: who typed it, `{chat, entity, account, admin}` (`chat` true: another player in the game's chat, `entity` 0 if unknown, `account` a text "0x" + 16 hex digits, `admin` (1.4) true when they may run every command: the console, the host, `[chat] admins`); the host's own chat and the console give `chat` false; nil outside commands
- `emf.session()`: a number that changes when a world loads (entity ids from an older session mean nothing)
- `emf.on_world_data(fn)` / `emf.save_world_data(text)` / `emf.player_data(a)` / `emf.save_player_data(a, text)`: your data for the world being played: `fn(world, text)` once after the world loaded / save text for it; (1.20) a text per player (see "Saving data")
- `emf.setting(key)`: one of your settings from `mod.json`: a `bool` as true/false, `int` and whole `slider` as an integer, `float` and decimal `slider` as a number, `choice` as its index, `select` as the option's value (text), `color` as `"#rrggbb"`, `keybind` as the key's name (`""`: none), `text` as text; players change them in the Mods tab and EMF.exe
- `emf.set_setting(key, value)` / `emf.on_setting_changed(fn)`: change one / `fn(key)` after each change
- `emf.item(name)` / `emf.item_info(id)`: an item's id by its debug name (`items wood` in the console lists names) / `{id, name, max_stack, guid}`; inside callbacks only (they need a world), so look ids up in your first `on_tick` or command
- `emf.item_name(item [, "game"])` / `emf.language()`: (1.21) the name the game shows for an item (an id or a debug name), in the player's language: `name, true`; `debug_name, false` where the game has none (the dedicated server, before its text is known, an older core); `nil, false` for an unknown item. For EMF's screens (windows, wheels, HUD lines) a name EMF's fonts cannot draw comes in English (Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Thai until EMF found a font for them, README_EMF.md); `"game"` gives the player's language always (for the chat). Inside callbacks only / `"en_us"`, `"de_de"`, ... or nil (reference.md "v29"); the `kill_counter` example shows its line in the player's language with it
- `emf.give(world, player, item, count)`: drops items at a player; `item` is an id or a name
- `emf.put(world, entity, item, count [, fn] [, {level = n, rarity = r}])`: puts items straight into an inventory; `fn(world, added)` one step later. The table (1.4, before or after `fn`): an item level for gear and a rarity, 0-4 or `"common"`, `"uncommon"`, `"rare"`, `"epic"`, `"legendary"` (without them: the game's defaults)
- `emf.take(world, entity, item, count [, fn] [, {slot = id, exact = true}])`: takes items out (all or nothing); `fn(world, taken)`. The table (1.6): `slot` an InventorySlotId (the inventory entity in the low 32 bits, the slot index 0-7 above: `inv
- `emf.move(world, from, to, item, count [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.6) moves items without losing any: take, put, give back, drop; `opts`: `slot`, `exact`, `fallback`, `level`, `rarity`; `fn(world, moved, returned, dropped, taken)`. true when started (see "Moving items" below)
- `emf.spawn(world, guid, x, y, z [, components])` / `emf.destroy(world, id)`: spawns a template at a position in metres / removes an entity (host only). 1.12: `components` = `{Name = {field = value}, ...}` are spawned with the entity (at most 15, by their real field names, absent fields 0; not `CurrentTransform`): `emf.spawn(w, guid, x, y, z, {ScaleComponent = {uniformScale = 1.25}})` makes a creature drawn 1.25x as big (a `ScaleComponent` from 0.1 to 10). An unknown name or field is an error. On a placed object `destroy` gives no item back, drops no loot and plays no pick-up sound; a container's contents go with it. Never destroy a Flame Altar (the base). For a pick-up use `emf.remove_building` (1.28); for loot use `emf.damage` on a `Destructible` object
- `emf.remove_building(world, id [, opts])`: 1.28: removes a placed object like a pick-up, item back; `true, item_id` or `false, reason`; options below
- `emf.path_find(world, from, to [, opts], fn)`: 1.29: asks the game's path grid for a path, `fn(world, result, points)` comes later; id or nil; options below
- `emf.path_cancel(id)`: 1.29: cancels an open path query; true when it was open
- `emf.door(world, id)`: 1.30: `"open"` or `"closed"` plus `{locked = bool, logic = bool}`, or nil when not a door (see "Doors" below)
- `emf.door_open(world, id [, "front" | "back"])` / `emf.door_close(world, id)`: 1.30: opens / closes a door at the next step; true when it will change, false when refused
- `emf.door_lock(world, id, locked)`: 1.30: no E prompt on the door while locked (kept with the world from EMF 0.6.8); true / false
- `emf.enemy_order(world, enemy, target [, opts])`: 1.32: the enemy goes for the target (a door, a gate, a creature, a player); the order's id, or nil and why (see "Enemy orders" below)
- `emf.enemy_order_cancel(id)` / `emf.enemy_target(world, enemy)`: 1.32: end an order / what the enemy goes for now (or nil)
- `emf.enemy_move(world, enemy, points [, opts] [, fn])`: 1.33: the creature walks to a point or through a list of points; the move's id, or nil and why (see "Move orders" below)
- `emf.enemy_move_cancel(id)` / `emf.enemy_moving(world, enemy)`: 1.33: end a move / its move's id now (or nil)
- `emf.kill(world, id)`: (1.4) kills a creature without a hit: its current health becomes 0 (1.5: through the game's attribute code) and the game's death program sends `EntityDiedEvent` the next step; the corpse keeps its loot. No attacker, no kill credit (`emf.damage` gives one); never a player; host only. true / false
- `emf.health(world, id)`: (1.5) the current and maximum health: `local cur, max = emf.health(w, id)`; the game's attributes in a world you host, else the replicated `NetworkHealth`; nil when neither is there
- `emf.attribute(world, id, attr)`: (1.5) an attribute as the game reads it: `attr` is `"health"`, `"max_health"`, `"stamina"`, `"max_stamina"`, `"mana"`, `"max_mana"`, a player's `"xp_pending"`, `"xp"`, `"xp_required"` and `"level"` (1.11, EMF API v22), or an attribute id; nil when the entity has none. Give XP with `emf.attribute_add(w, player, "xp_pending", n)`: the game levels the player up itself (the other three are read-only). Host only
- `emf.attribute_add(world, id, attr, delta)`: (1.5) adds `delta` (a whole number) through the game's own attribute code: damage stops at 0, a heal of `"health"`, `"stamina"` or `"mana"` at its maximum (other heals are refused). Not a hit: no kill credit, no hit reaction. Host only. true / false
- `emf.damage(world, attacker, target, amount)`: (1.5) `amount` of true damage as a real game hit on the next step: a `HitEvent` (damage numbers, always a light reaction, aggro toward the attacker), the killing blow, kill credit and XP for `attacker` when it is a player (0 = no attacker, no aggro). The target must take hits (creatures and players, and since 1.23 placed objects: see "Hits" below) and not be immune. Host only. true / false
- `emf.xp_required(world, level)`: (1.11) the XP `level` needs before the next one (the game's own curve); nil outside 1..cap or when unknown. Host only
- `emf.level_cap(world)`: (1.11) the highest level a player can reach; nil when unknown. Host only
- `emf.set_level(world, player, level [, xp])`: (1.11) sets a player's level (1..cap) with `xp` (default 0) towards the next one: raises or lowers at once, without level-up events (to level up the game's way, give XP with `emf.attribute_add(w, player, "xp_pending", n)`). The skill points follow the level; after lowering, a skill tree that costs more points than the level gives is reset by the game at the next load. Saved with the character. Host only. true (done or queued) / false
- `emf.add_component(world, id, name [, data] [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.12) adds component `name` to entity `id` through the game's own command, with `data` = `{field = value}` by the real field names (absent fields are 0; pass `nil` for `data` to give `opts` or `fn` without it). In this version only `ScaleComponent` (`uniformScale` from 0.1 to 10) and `InteractionPause`; the components the world save keeps are refused until checked in game ([reference.md](reference.md), "v23"). A `ScaleComponent` added this way is not drawn (the game reads the size when it makes the creature): spawn with it instead (`emf.spawn`'s `components`). Only when absent: one already there is never overwritten. Never a player. Applied two server steps later; `fn(world, status, why)` then runs once: `status` is `"done"`, `"already"` or `"failed"` (not called when the world ends first). An unknown name or field is an error. Host only. true (queued) / false (refused: see the log; `fn` is not called)
- `emf.remove_component(world, id, name [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.12) removes component `name` from entity `id`: one this mod added in this session (`ScaleComponent`, `InteractionPause`). `fn` as above (`"already"`: it was not there). Host only. true / false
- `emf.tell(world, id, text [, opts])`: (1.6) a chat line only player `id` sees, under their own name (in a game you host, a note for the host itself); (1.22) `opts` `{system = true}`: shown with no name, like the game's "joined" lines, also with text chat off (a label only as a prefix: `"[Raid] ..."`; an older core shows it under the player's name); `"\n"` splits lines, at most 10. Where players' chat is on: a dedicated server, or `[chat] players=1` in a game you host ([server.md](server.md)). A Lua mod may send 30 lines in 10 s. true when queued, false when refused (the log says why)
- `emf.broadcast(text [, opts])`: (1.6) the same line for every connected player (a note for the host of a game you host); (1.22) `opts` as `emf.tell`. true / false
- `emf.on_chat(fn)`: (1.6) `fn(world, account, entity, text)` for every chat line a player sends that is not an EMF command, on the server world after its next step; `account` as text ("0x" + 16 hex digits), `entity` 0 when unknown. Read-only: the line is shown as usual. false where players' chat is off
- `emf.request_save()`: (1.6) asks the game to save the world now (the save its 30 s timer makes). Host or dedicated server. true when asked
- `emf.teleport(world, id, x, y, z [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.7) moves an entity as fast travel does (see "Teleport" below)
- `emf.world_settings.get(key)`, `.set(key, value [, persist])`, `.reset([key] [, persist])`, `.list()`: (1.10) the running world's settings: day length, loot, XP, enemy damage... (see "World settings" below). Host or dedicated server
- `emf.on_world_setting_changed(fn)`: (1.10) `fn(key, value)` once per world setting the server wrote, whoever changed it, on the server world after that step. false on an older core
- `emf.time_of_day([world])`: (1.4) the time of day in hours (`19.5` = 19:30) from the world's clock, or nil when it is not known. Inside callbacks only (it needs a world: the callback's, or the one you pass); at the top of `main.lua` it is an error, as `emf.item` is
- `emf.session_token()`: (1.4) a text that names this run of the game and its hosted session. Save it with entity ids: `emf.session()` restarts at 1 every time the game starts and the ids are renumbered, so only a matching token means the ids still name the same entities
- `emf.on_key(key, fn [, "server"/"client"])`: `fn(world)` once per press of `key`: one of your `keybind` settings (the player's choice counts, also when changed while the game runs) or a key name (`"F7"`, `"G"`). It runs after the next step of the server world when your game hosts one, else of your client world (or of the kind given). Keys only count while the game window is in front and the console is closed
- `emf.key_down(key)`: true while the key (or the key in a `keybind` setting) is held
- `emf.wheel(title, labels, key, fn)`: the radial wheel; `key` is held to choose (`"G"`, `""` for click); `fn(world, choice)`, choice 1..n or nil
- `emf.wheel_section(group, title, labels, fn)`: (1.9) your part of a wheel shared by several mods: publishes (replaces) your section of `group`; an empty list or nil removes it. `fn(world, index, label)` gets the index into the labels as they were when the wheel opened, and the label shown: if you published another list since, find the item by `label`. A pick from a wheel opened before your mod reloaded is dropped. Publish again when your labels change
- `emf.wheel_group(group, title, key)`: (1.9) opens one wheel with every mod's section of `group` (each label as "Section: label" when more than one mod has a section); a pick runs only its owner's `fn`. True when it opened (false: no labels, or more than 64)
- `emf.on_hit(fn [, {kinds = ...}])`: (1.23) `fn(world, hit)` after the server applied each landing hit on an entity (the game's `HitEvent`), on the server world; with `kinds` also fall, shroud, cold and drowning damage; see "Hits" below. Joined players' games see none. true / false (false on an older core)
- `emf.hit_rule{from, to, crit, backstab, weakspot, types, attack, healing, kinds, scale, add, min_health, cancel}`: (1.23) a rule the core applies to every matching hit before it lands: change its amount or cancel it. Returns its id, or nil when refused (the log says why: 64 rules, the hook not usable on this game build). See "Hits" below
- `emf.hit_rule_remove(id)`: (1.23) removes a rule of this script. true only for the script's own rule
- `emf.buff_types(world [, slot])`: (1.24) the game's buff types as a list of type tables; `slot` is `"food"`, `"buff"`, `"debuff"`, `"rested"` or `"terrain"`. Any world. See "Buffs" below
- `emf.buff_type(world, id)`: (1.24) one type table, or nil
- `emf.buffs(world, entity)`: (1.24) the entity's active buffs as a list of tables, in slot order. Any world
- `emf.apply_buff(world, target, type [, {seconds, source, item}] [, fn(world, result)])`: (1.24) gives a buff through the game's own buff code in the next step; `fn` gets the result after it. Server world only. true when queued, false when refused at once (logged)
- `emf.remove_buff(world, target, type [, fn(world, result)])`: (1.24) removes a buff the game's way (a cleanse: gone after the next step). Server world only. true / false as `emf.apply_buff`
- `emf.on_buff(fn)`: (1.24) `fn(world, ev)` after the server step for every change of a player's buffs: applied, refreshed, removed. false on an older core
- `emf.marker(id, spec)` / `emf.remove_marker(id)` / `emf.clear_markers()`: (1.25) a marker over the 3D view and on the map on this game. See "Markers" below
- `emf.send_marker(player, id, spec)` / `emf.unsend_marker(player, id)`: (1.25) server: a marker on a player's game (nil: every player's); players need EMF
- `emf.world_to_screen(x, y, z)` / `emf.marker_types()`: (1.25) a world point in display pixels (or nil) / the game's map icon types seen in this world
- `emf.map_cursor()` / `emf.on_map_click(fn)`: (1.26) the world spot under the mouse on the open map (or nil) / a function for clicks on the map. See "The map" below
- `emf.map_action(id, opts, fn)` / `emf.remove_map_action(id)`: (1.26) server: something players do on their map by holding Shift and the left mouse button; players need EMF
- `emf.ground_at(world, x, z, fn)`: (1.26) server world: the ground height under a spot, answered a moment later
- `emf.player_view()` / `emf.fog_at(x, z)` / `emf.map_markers()`: (1.27) the local player's position and heading / the fog of war at a point / the game's own map markers. See "Canvases and the minimap" below
- `emf.canvas(id, spec)` / `emf.canvas_draw(id, list)`: (1.27) a drawing panel EMF draws over the HUD / its drawing
- `emf.on_player_joined(fn)`, `emf.on_player_left(fn)`, `emf.on_player_died(fn)`: (1.20) `fn(world, p)` on the server world, `p` = `{player, account, name, host, killer}` (`killer`: died only, the last hitter within 10 s or 0). All join 1 s after the world data; died needs the call in the first run. False on an older core (reference.md "v28")
- `emf.net.channel(name, def)`: (1.19) a message channel `"<mod id>/<name>"`: `def` = `{version, to = "server" | "players" | "both", max, per_10s, on_server = fn(world, from, data), on_player = fn(world, from, data)}`; `from` = `{player, account, admin, is_local, version}`. A reload binds the new functions; a new version needs a restart. In process, and to joined players and the server over the chat (reference.md "v27")
- `emf.net.send(name, data)`, `.send_to(world, player, name, data)`, `.send_all(world, name, data)`, `.peer(world, player, name)`: (1.19) to the server (true: sent) / to one player's game / to all with the channel (count) / that game's channel version (`peer(nil, 0, name)`: the server's; 0 = none)
- `emf.offered(world, id)`: (1.15) true while your script's offer on `id` is in EMF's hands (not removed, not dropped by EMF); after a drop, `emf.offer` again takes it back
- `emf.image(path)`: (1.15) a picture for windows: a .png or a folder of .png frames inside your mod's folder (`"pics/wolf.png"`, `"pics/wolf_turn"`), or `"portrait:<key>"` (EMF's portrait cache); the handle for a row's `image` or `icon`, or 0 (refused: logged; a core before v26), which a row takes as no picture and keeps its place. A path that leaves your mod's folder is an error. reference.md "v26"
- `emf.window(id, def, fn)`: (1.13) opens a window EMF's overlay draws (one at a time; it takes the mouse and keyboard; Esc, its `close_key` or its X close it); true when it opened. `id` gets your mod's id in front (`"stable"` is `"beastmaster.stable"`). `def`: `title`, `width` (in text heights, about 28 by default), `place` (`"centre"`, `"left"`, `"right"`), `close_key` (a key name, for example `emf.setting("stable_key")`), `world` (`"server"` when you host, else `"client"`: where `fn` runs), `rows` = a list, top to bottom, each one of `{text = ...}`, `{heading = ...}`, `{button = key, text = ...}`, `{row = key, text = "Name (detail)"}`, `{slot = key, text = ..., count = n}`, `{bar = text, value = 0..1}`, `{separator = true}`, `{image = emf.image(...), height = 6, fps = 12, key = ...}` (1.15), with `icon = emf.image(...)` and `fps` on slots and rows (1.15), and any of `same_line`, `selected`, `disabled`, `dim`, `empty`, `locked` (true), `tooltip` and `color` (`"#rrggbb"`). `fn(world, ev)`: `ev.kind` is `"click"`, `"right_click"` or, last, `"closed"` (with `ev.reason` `"player"`, `"mod"` or `"core"`); `ev.key` is the clicked row's key. A reload closes the script's window. An unknown row kind or field is an error. false (logged) while another window or a wheel is open, with no world of its kind, without the overlay (a dedicated server). `close_key = ""` (a key setting left unset) is no close key
- `emf.window_update(id, def)`: (1.13) new contents for your open window (`fn` stays); false when it is not open (the player closed it): it never reopens one
- `emf.window_close(id)`: (1.13) closes your window (`fn` gets `"closed"`, reason `"mod"`); false when it is not open
- `emf.offer(world, id [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.14) the game's own "E <verb>" prompt on entity `id` of the server world you host; `fn(world, player, entity)` runs when any player presses E there. `opts`: `verb` (`"Use"` (default), `"Open"`, `"Talk"`, `"Read"`, `"Sit"`, `"Sleep"`, `"Pet"`, `"Touch"`, `"Activate"`, `"Press"`, `"Enter"`, `"Inspect"`, `"Take"`, `"Collect"`, `"Rest"`, `"Release"` or a loca id), `text` (your own words, shown once a content mod adds them with `add_prompt_words`, content.md; else "E" with no word), `sequence` (`"touch"`, `"button"`), `range`, `low_priority`, `build_mode`. false for a player or an entity with the game's or another mod's offer. Offer again after a load; a reload takes the script's offers off. Host only (reference.md "v25")
- `emf.spawn_offer(world, guid, x, y, z [, opts] [, fn])`: (1.14) spawns a template with an offer on it (`emf.offer`'s options); the entity id, or nil. The prop may stay in the save without its offer: after a load offer it again, don't spawn another
- `emf.offer_remove(world, id)`: (1.14) takes your script's offer off the entity; false when it has none of yours
- `emf.emits(names [, kind])` / `emf.emit(kind, name, fields)`: send engine events (see below)
- `world:is_server()`, `world:is_client()`: which world: gameplay changes go to the server world (the host)
- `world:tick()`: its tick counter
- `world:entities()`: every entity id (a table)
- `world:position(id)`: `x, y, z` in metres, or nil
- `world:get(component, id)`: the entity's component, or nil
- `world:template(component, id)`: (1.8) the entity's template half of a component: the data every entity of its template shares (for example `world:template("ModelResource", id).model`, the model GUID as text). Read-only: writing a field is an error. nil when the entity has none
- `world:name(id)`: (1.6) a player's name, the one the game's chat shows (their platform name, not the character's), or nil (then say `"player #" .. id`); where players' chat is on, server world only
- `world:character_name(id)`: (1.22) the player's character name (the Social tab's), or nil when not known: it may already be there in `on_player_joined` or come a few seconds later, and it can change during a session, so read it when you need it and never keep it. Text a player's game set, not an identity: key data by `p.account`. Server world only; players' chat need not be on
- `world:account(id)`: a player entity's account as text ("0x" + 16 hex digits, as `emf.sender()` gives it), or nil: a key that stays the same for that player across sessions (entity ids do not); server world only

## mod.json (docs/modding/reference.md)

- `id`: required; 1-48 of `a-z 0-9 _ . -`; names the settings file and section (`emf\config\<id>.ini`, `[<id>]`)
- `version`: required; `"1"`, `"1.2"` or `"1.2.3"`
- `name`, `description`, `authors`: shown in the Mods tab and by `mods` (`authors` is a list of texts)
- `dll`: the DLL in the folder (default `<id>.dll`); `main` instead names a script for a script host (Lua)
- `emf`: the lowest `EMF_API_VERSION` the mod needs (a whole number); a newer one than the core's: not loaded
- `depends`: the mods yours needs, with a version range each (below): `{"lua": ">=1.3", "helper": {"version": "~2.1", "optional": true}}`, or a list `[{"id": "helper", "version": "^2.0", "optional": true}, "other"]` (ShroudForge's form; its name `"dependencies"` works too, but not both). Yours loads after them; it does not load when a required one is missing, the wrong version, switched off or failed, and the Mods tab says which and why. An `optional` one may be missing or off; when it runs, it loads first and its version must fit.
- `enabled`: the switch's value while the ini has none (default `true`)
- `settings`: a list of settings, shown in the Mods tab and in EMF.exe (below)
- `side`: where the mod has to run, for people who host a dedicated server: `"server"` (on the server or the host only; players do not need it), `"client"` (in a player's own game only: HUD lines, keys, notes; on a dedicated server it does nothing) or `"both"` (the server and every player need it). Optional: without it a mod counts as `"both"`, unknown. EMF loads the mod everywhere either way; the field only drives EMF.exe's notes for a server folder ("Players need this mod too", "Does nothing on a server", a warning for a client mod switched on there; docs/app.md "Servers"). Another value is a warning in EMF.exe, not an error. An EML mod's `mod.json` may say it too

Version ranges in depends (SemVer, like npm/Cargo):
`"*"` = any version; `"^1.2.0"`, `"^1.2"` = 1.2.0 up to below 2.0.0 (`^0.2.3`: below 0.3.0; `^0.0.3`: only 0.0.3); `"~1.2.3"`, `"~1.2"` = 1.2.3 / 1.2.0 up to below 1.3.0 (`~1`: below 2.0.0); `"1.2.3"`, `"1.2"` = a bare version: the same as `^` (that version or a compatible newer one); `">=1.1"`, `">1.2"`, `"<2"`, `"<=1.2"` = comparisons; `>1.2` is newer than every 1.2.x, `<=1.2` up to every 1.2.x; `"=1.2.3"` = exactly that version (`=1.2` is exactly 1.2.0); `"1.2.x"`, `"1.*"` = any number in place of the `x`; `"1.2.3 - 2.0.0"`, `"1.2 - 2"` = both ends included; a shorter end takes its whole family (`1.2 - 2`: 1.2.0 up to every 2.x, below 3.0.0); `">=1.0, <2.0"`, `">=1.0 <2.0"` = all must hold; `"^1.0 || ^2.0"` = either side

Settings: each entry of "settings" takes key (1-48 of A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -; "enabled" is reserved), type,
default, label, help, live (true: applied at once), group (a heading), enabledWhen ({"setting": k, "equals": v}).
Kinds:
- `bool`: shown as a switch; stored as `1` / `0`; Lua: true / false
- `int`, `float`: shown as a number box, or a slider when `min` and `max` are both given (for `int`: at most 1,000,000 apart, or with `"control": "slider"`); fields `min`, `max`, `step`, `control`; stored as the number; Lua: integer / number; a fraction for an `int` is refused (from the ini: rounded)
- `slider`: shown as a slider; fields `min` and `max` (required), `step`; stored as **a whole number only with a whole `step`** (and whole `min`, `max`, `default`): `"step": 1`; without a step, or with a fractional one, a decimal. A value between steps moves to the nearest step. For a whole-number slider you can also write `"type": "int", "control": "slider"`
- `choice`: shown as a list; fields `choices`: `["top right", "bottom left"]` (default by index or text); stored as the index; Lua: integer
- `select`: shown as a list; fields `options`: `["a", "b"]` or `[{"value": "tr", "label": "Top right"}]` (default by value or label); stored as the option's value; Lua: text
- `keybind` (or `key`): shown as a key: click it, then press a key (EMF.exe and the Mods tab); Shift, Ctrl or Alt bind when pressed and released alone (Shift+G binds G); EMF.exe binds the key the game sees (with NumLock off, Numpad 8 is Up); stored as a key name as `emf/keys.hpp` reads it (`G`, `F7`, `Space`, `Numpad5`, `0xba`); `""` = no key. A default that is no key refuses that setting (logged); the mod still loads
- `color`: shown as a colour picker; stored as `#rrggbb` (`#rgb` and any case are read); C++: `emf::setting_rgba` for `emf::hud`; Lua: the text, which `emf.hud` takes
- `text`: shown as a text field; fields `maxLength` (1-256 characters); stored as the text: one line, at most 256 bytes, no spaces or quotes around it

## Console commands

Typed into the in-game console (key under Esc), the bridge's console command, or <game>\emf\commands.txt
(read about once a second while a world runs). (host) = needs a world you host.
help, mods, settings, set, hooks, pattern, hud.list, hud.move, hud.scale, hud.hide, hud.show, hud.reset, hud.layout, hud.swap, hud.order, hud.colour, hud.grow, profile, saves.backup, saves.list also work at the main menu.

- help [page]: list the commands (in the chat 8 per page)
- mods: list the mods and what became of them
- settings <mod>: list a mod's settings
- hooks: every inline hook, its owner and target (EMF's and mods')
- pattern <bytes> [.section]: test a byte pattern against the game exe (found once?)
- set <mod> <key> <value>: change a mod's setting (saved in emf/config/<mod>.ini)
- items [words]: find the game's items by name (words in any order, part of a word is enough)
- give <item name> [count]: drop items at your feet (host)
- put <item name> [count 1-65535] [entity] [level] [rarity 0-4]: put items straight into an inventory, yours by default (host)
- take <item name> [count 1-65535] [entity]: take items out of an inventory, yours by default (host)
- spawn <item name | template guid> [count 1-20] [at <x> <y> <z>]: what a placeable item puts down (or a template), in front of you or at a place (host)
- time <hours 0-24>: set the time of day (host)
- pos: your position
- perf: how long the game's world steps, EMF's wait and each mod took per step since the last perf
- goto [#k] <x> <y> <z> | <entity> [ground] (host)
- near [radius 1-200]: the entities around you, nearest first, and what they are (host)
- hud <id> [place 0-2] [text]: keep a line on screen (0 top right, 1 bottom right, 2 bottom left); no text removes it
- inv <entity>: every stack in the entity's inventories, with slot ids and gear levels (host)
- health <entity> [percent 1-100]: a creature's or player's health; with a percent, set it to that share of its maximum, e.g. a beast beaten down for taming (host)
- ai <entity>: what a creature's AI does: its state, whom it guards and fights, its aggro and faction (host)
- order <enemy> <target> [seconds] [damage]: the enemy goes for the target (a door, a gate, a creature, a player); damage is added to each of its hits on it (host)
- order.stop <id>: end an order (host)
- move <enemy> <x> <y> <z> [peaceful] | <enemy> <entity | me> [peaceful]: the enemy walks there (its own way, jumps if its kind can); peaceful: it ignores players (host)
- move.stop <id>: end a move (host)
- entities: count the entities in the server world
- inspect <entity>: list the entity's components (template ones marked)
- tpl <entity> <component> [bytes 1-256] [offset]: hex dump of the entity's template data
- tplset <entity> <component> <offset> <f32|i32|u32|u16|u8> <value>: change one template value (host)
- stack <item name> <max 1-65535>: change an item's stack size until the game restarts (host)
- door <entity> [open|close|lock|unlock] [front|back]: a door's state, or open, close or lock it (host)
- path <x> <y> <z> [jumps] [closest] [nodes]: a path from you on the game's path grid (it moves nothing; host)
- remove <entity> [me|drop|<player>] [force]: take a placed object away like a pick-up, its item back to you, as a drop or to a player; refused for a chest with items unless force (they drop on the ground), and for a Flame Altar (host)
- destroy <entity>: remove an entity from the world, never a player (host)
- hud.list: the HUD editor's state, every HUD part with its offset, scale and whether it is hidden, and the layouts
- hud.move <part> <x> <y>: move a HUD part, in percent of the screen from where the game draws it (e.g. hud.move vitals 5 -2.5)
- hud.scale <part> <0.5-2>: a HUD part's size, around the screen edge it is nearest (e.g. hud.scale hotbar 0.75)
- hud.hide <part>: hide a HUD part (hud.show brings it back)
- hud.show <part>: show a hidden HUD part again
- hud.reset [part]: put one HUD part, or every part, back where the game draws it
- hud.layout [save|load|delete <name>]: the HUD layouts in emf\\hud (save as a new name, switch, delete); without words, the list
- hud.swap health|mana|stamina health|mana|stamina: two of the vitals' bars change places (e.g. hud.swap health mana: mana on top)
- hud.order <bar> <bar> <bar>: the vitals' bars from the top (e.g. hud.order mana health stamina)
- hud.colour [bar] [part] [colour]: the vitals' bar colours (e.g. hud.colour health #ff4040, hud.colour mana empty #00000000, hud.colour panel #20202080, hud.colour health game)
- hud.grow up|down: the status effects list grows upward from the food icons' bottom edge, or down as the game draws it
- profile [save <name> [--settings] [--replace] | load <name>]: mod profiles (the mods' switches by name; a load applies at the next game start)
- saves.backup [label]: back up every save file now (at the main menu)
- saves.list: the save backups, newest first, and where they are

From the mods in the EMF zip (only while that mod runs):
- companion.gear: what the companion wears and the level it gets [companion]
- companion.aim: the camera ray and the creatures near it (why Attack picks what it picks) [companion]
- quick_stack: put what you carry into the nearby chests that hold it [quick_stack]
- qs: put what you carry into the nearby chests that hold it [quick_stack]
- qs.chests: the sorting chests, recyclers and overflow chests near you [quick_stack]
- qs.mark sort|recycle|overflow|none [chest]: mark the chest you look at, or that entity (host; chat: the nearest within 3 m) [quick_stack]
- qs.list: every marked chest of this world (host) [quick_stack]
- lua.status: every Lua mod and whether it runs [lua]
- lua.perf: how long each Lua mod took per world step since the last lua.perf [lua]
- lua.reload: reload the Lua mods whose files changed (this also happens every second) [lua]
- loot.toggle [on|off]: your Loot Magnet (corpses of creatures killed near you come to you) [loot_magnet]
- loot.status: is your Loot Magnet on, and its rules [loot_magnet]
- sleep.status: who is asleep, and whether the day is being skipped [sleep]
- sleep.pretend [on|off]: every player counts as asleep (host, for tests) [sleep]
- herald.say <text>: a line for everyone [herald]
- herald.tell <name|#k> <text>: a line for one player (#k as /players numbers them) [herald]
- herald.restart <minutes> [reason]: count down to a restart (10, 5, 2, 1 min, 30 s); the stop is outside EMF [herald]
- herald.cancel: stop the restart countdown [herald]
- herald.save: save the world now [herald]
- herald.seen <name>: when a player was last on this world, and their playtime [herald]
- herald.reload: read announcements.txt and webhook.txt again [herald]
- players: who is online, and for how long [herald]
- playtime: your playtime on this world, and your rank [herald]
- motd: the message of the day [herald]
- unstuck: a hop to free ground, else a /home [teleports]
- home: to your spawn point [teleports]
- tp <#k|name> [<#m|name>]: to k, or k to m (admin) [teleports]
- bring <#k|name>: to you (admin) [teleports]
- tp.pos [#k] <x> <y> <z> [ground] (admin) [teleports]
- tp.back [#k]: undo the last teleport (admin) [teleports]
- tp.list: the players' #k (admin) [teleports]
- tp.mark [#k]: to your map waypoint (#k: player k to theirs, admin) [teleports]
- craft <n|max> [name]: more of what you crafted by hand here [bulk_craft]
- craft.stop: stop your order [bulk_craft]
- craft.list: what you can bulk-craft here [bulk_craft]
- craft.teach <recipe hex> [player]: as if crafted by hand (host) [bulk_craft]
- blessings <god|refill|stamina|mana|nofall|heal|off|xp|level|list|help> [on|off|n|undo] [#k|name]: Flame Blessings (admin) [blessings]
- jobs: the villagers' jobs [villager_jobs]
- job <villager> <chest> <recipe id hex>: give a villager a job (host) [villager_jobs]
- job.stop <villager>: end a villager's job [villager_jobs]
- job.recall [villager]: unstick a villager (host) [villager_jobs]
- job.recipes <villager> [chest]: what the villager can make (from the chest) [villager_jobs]
- job.farm <villager> <chest>: farm the crops around the chest (host) [villager_jobs]
- job.tend <villager> <chest>: tend the animals around the chest (host) [villager_jobs]
- job.haul <villager> <from chest> <to chest>: carry items between two chests (host) [villager_jobs]
- job.gather <villager> <chest>: gather the wild pickables around the chest into it (host) [villager_jobs]
- raids.status: is Night Raids on in this world, and the raid going on [raids]
- raids.start [warning seconds]: a raid now at the base with the most players (host, for tests) [raids]
- raids.stop: end the raid; its raiders are removed (host) [raids]
- raids.world on|off: Night Raids in this world (host; every world starts off) [raids]
- raids.kill: every living raider dies (host, for tests; they count as slain) [raids]
- kill_counter.reset: count from 0 again [kill_counter]
- life_skills.skills: your life skills [life_skills]
- champion.where: where the champion is, from you [champion]
- champion.stats: champions slain in this world [champion]
- champion.summon [metres]: a champion now, near you (host, for tests) [champion]
- champion.dismiss: the champion leaves now (host) [champion]
- champion.kill: the champion dies now (host, for tests: no hit, the nearest player is rewarded) [champion]
- bounty.board: the notices and your bounties [bounty]
- bounty.take <n>: take notice n [bounty]
- bounty.drop <n>: give up your bounty n [bounty]
- bounty.claim: your finished bounties' rewards [bounty]
- bounty.reroll <n>: swap your notice n [bounty]
- bounty.top: who finished the most [bounty]
- bounty.give <id>: hold a bounty now (tests) [bounty]
- bounty.reset: new notices now [bounty]
- bounty.mark: the prop you look at is a Bounty Board [bounty]
- bounty.unmark: the marked prop nearest you is no board [bounty]
- bounty.boards: this world's Bounty Boards [bounty]
- grave.where: where your tombstone is [grave]
- grave.claim: your tombstone's items come to you [grave]
- grave.list: every known tombstone and its owner (host) [grave]
- grave.adopt: the nearest tombstone within 10 m becomes yours (host; for tombstones from before Grave Keeper ran) [grave]
- handover <item> [count|all]: hand items to the nearest player within reach (/handover.who lists them) [handover]
- handover.who: the players within reach of you, numbered for /handover.to [handover]
- handover.block [on|off]: refuse (or accept again) items others hand you [handover]
- handover.to <name|#k> <item> [count|all]: hand items to that player (within reach) [handover]
- handover.log: the last hand-overs [handover]
- handover.debug_target <entity|off>: (tests) every hand-over goes to this villager or chest [handover]
- beastmaster.species <animation graph guid> <faction number> [scale]: which beast a creature is (for modders) [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.stable mark | unmark | list: the prop you look at is a stable; the marked prop nearest you is not; this world's stables (host and admins) [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.threat: the monsters held on you or your beasts now, and for how long [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.home: where your beasts at home are (in a Large Stable) and what they do [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.idle: what your beasts do while you stand still now [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.loyalty <name or number> <1-10>: set a beast's loyalty (admin) [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.give <species>: add a beast to your collection (admin) [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.spawn <species>: a wild beast 5 m in front of you, to try taming (admin) [beastmaster]
- beastmaster.as <#k or player entity> <word> [...]: run a player's word as that player: give, loyalty, open [name], or any /beastmaster word (console only; for tests on a dedicated server) [beastmaster]
Lua mods add <id>.<name> commands with emf.command.

## Debug bridge (docs/modding/debug_bridge.md)

Off unless <game>\emf\emf_core.ini has [debug] bridge=1 (scripts\install_emf.ps1 -Bridge). A named pipe
\\.\pipe\emf-bridge-<pid> for this Windows user only; <game>\emf\bridge.txt names it. One JSON object per line:
request {"id": n, "cmd": "...", ...}; reply {"id": n, "ok": true, ...} or {"id": n, "ok": false, "code": c,
"error": "..."} with code timeout | busy | unavailable | bad_request | unknown_command | refused. Pushed events
(no id): {"event": "log" | "game" | "dropped", ...}. Clients: scripts\emf_bridge.ps1, tools/bridge/emf_bridge.py.

- hello: Replies {"id":1,"ok":true,"emf":"0.3.0","api":16,"game_build":1273043,"process":"client","pid":4242,"protocol":1, "commands":["hello","console",...],"events":["pickup","kill","damage","save","load"],"max_clients":8} e.g. {"id":1,"cmd":"hello"}
- console: Runs the line exactly as if you typed it into the console and answers with what happened: {"id":2,"ok":true,"status":"ran","output":["put 1 x Material_T1_Wood_Logs into entity 1: 1 added"],"log_seq":1834} e.g. {"id":2,"cmd":"console","text":"put Material_T1_Wood_Logs 1"}
- state: Answers with one snapshot: {"id":3,"ok":true, "world":{"status":"running","kind":"server","tick":51234,"ecs_time_s":853.9,"time_of_day_h":13.25,"slot":1, "name":"<world name>"}, "character":{"storage":"local","slot":1,"name":"<character ... e.g. {"id":3,"cmd":"state"}
- mods: Answers {"mods":[...]}: every mod with id, name, version, status (loaded, failed, disabled, not loaded, script, loading), reason, source, authors and enabled_default. e.g. {"id":4,"cmd":"mods"}
- log: EMF keeps the last 5000 log lines in memory, numbered from 1. {"id":5,"cmd":"log"}: the last 100 lines. {"id":5,"cmd":"log","since":1200}: the lines after line 1200 (at most max, 1 to 5000, default 1000). The reply: {"lines":[{"seq":1201,"line":"[20:15:00.123 t01234] ..."}],"last":1300,"more":false,"following":false}. With "more": true, ask again with "since": <last>. When lines after since are gone already, the reply ... "follow": true also pushes every new line: {"event":"log","seq":1301,"line":"..."}. A follower that fell more than 5000 lines behind gets "missed": <n> on the next line. "follow": false stops it. e.g. {"id":5,"cmd":"log"} {"id":5,"cmd":"log","since":1200}
- wait: Answers {"ok":true} once a world runs, or {"ok":false,"code":"timeout","error":"timed out"}. "for": "world": a world runs (yours or someone else's). "for": "player": a world runs and the local player exists. "for": "log", "match": "<text>": a log line contains the text (case matters). Only lines that come after the request count, unless you give "since": <line number> (0 searches every kept line; a console reply's log_se ... e.g. {"id":6,"cmd":"wait","for":"world","timeout_ms":120000}
- events: Pushes those game events to this client; "names": [] stops them. e.g. {"id":7,"cmd":"events","names":["pickup","kill"]}
- screenshot: Copies the next frame the game shows into a PNG and answers {"ok":true,"path":"C:\\...\\emf\\screens\\2026-10-26_20-15-00-123.png","width":1920,"height":1080,"hdr":false}. e.g. {"id":8,"cmd":"screenshot"}
- mod_key: Presses L for mods and answers after the release: {"ok":true,"key":"L","vk":76,"action":"press","mod_reads":9}. e.g. {"id":9,"cmd":"mod_key","key":"L"}
- quit: Answers {"ok":true,"quitting":true}, then asks the game's window to close (as its close button does): the game saves and exits a few seconds later. e.g. {"id":10,"cmd":"quit"}
- load_world: Starts a **LOCAL** save offline from the main menu, without clicks, the way "Play, Start a Session, Start..., Offline: Start" does, and answers once the world runs and the local player is in it: {"ok":true,"slot":1,"character":1,"world" ... e.g. {"id":11,"cmd":"load_world","slot":1,"character":1,"expect_name":"<character name>"}
- join: Joins a server with a **LOCAL** character, for tests with a dedicated server on the same PC. e.g. {"id":12,"cmd":"join","character":1,"expect_name":"<character name>","password":"<password>"}

## Tools for agents (docs/modding/ai_agents.md)

- scripts\game_session.ps1 start | stop | status -LockOwner <you>: installs the dev build with the bridge, starts
  the game, stops at the menu for a character check (exit 2; then start -Character local), loads the LOCAL test
  world through the bridge's load_world (no clicks; menu clicks for a 3840x2160 screen only on a build without
  it), and afterwards quits, uninstalls and checks the saves. It acts only on the game it recorded.
- tools/bridge/emf_scenario.py <scenario.json>: runs a JSON scenario (tests/game/*.json) through the bridge;
  exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 no game, 3 invalid file. {"name": ..., "load_world": {slot, character, expect_name}
  (optional: the load_world steps' defaults), "steps": [{"do": <kind>, ...}]}. Kinds:
  - hello (expect): the game answers: EMF, API and game build
  - wait (for*, match, since, timeout_s): wait for a world, the local player, or a log line
  - console (text*, expect, expect_re, status, timeout_s, settle_ms): run a console command and check its output
  - state (path*, op*, value, timeout_s): check a value in the game's state
  - mods (id*, status): a mod is listed (and has a status)
  - mod_key (key*, action, hold_ms, min_reads): press a key for mods (not the game)
  - screenshot (name, overlay, max_width): take a screenshot and copy it into the output folder
  - sleep (s*): wait a fixed time
  - edit_file (path*, find, replace, all, write): change a mod's file (put back at the end)
  - restore_file (path*): put an edited file back now
  - log_mark (name*): remember the newest log line
  - log_since_mark (mark*, match, match_re, absent, timeout_s): check the log lines after a mark
  - load_world (slot, character, expect_name, timeout_s): start a LOCAL save from the main menu, without clicks (passes at once when it runs already)
  (* = required; state paths: player.position.x, overlay.hud[id=clock.time].text, mods[0].id; ops: exists missing == != < > <= >= contains matches)
- tools/mcp/emf_mcp.py: an MCP server (stdio) with the tools emf_hello, emf_console, emf_state, emf_mods, emf_log, emf_wait, emf_screenshot, emf_mod_key, emf_run_scenario, emf_load_world; the repository's .mcp.json registers it.
  The tools that change the game (console, mod_key, run_scenario, load_world) act only on the game game_session
  recorded (--any-game for your own) and only at the main menu or in a LOCAL save played with a LOCAL character
  (state.character.storage "local"; a Steam or unknown character refuses them; --allow-cloud-world). The scenario
  runner's console, mod_key and edit_file steps follow the same rule.
